title: Brushes are picked from a library of tiles that each show that brush's real stroke
goal: Picking a brush should be visual: a grid of tiles grouped by kind (sketch, ink, paint, airbrush, texture), each tile showing a sample stroke painted live by that very brush in the current colour, so you can see what you get before you pick it. It replaces the plain Medium dropdown. Picking a tile arms that brush and shows its own settings.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-24: "I'd love a better brush selector" and "There should also be a better chooser than a dropdown without previewing."

Today: Sources/Photonz/ToolSettingsCapsule.swift:211-215 is a plain Picker("Medium") over BrushMedium.allCases. The mocks already designed this: brush-library.html (tiles in the Library group, scope Brushes, groups All, Sketch, Ink, Paint, Airbrush, Texture, Custom; picking repaints the sample stroke and drives Properties) and brush-editor.html. Mocks are the floor (objectives.json principles). The mock's Custom group, importing a brush file and making a brush from a selection are NOT part of this task unless they fall out cheaply; file them as follow-ups if they clear the bar.

Contradiction to settle: each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op (6.5) asks for 'a Medium dropdown with the seven media'. This task wins on how a brush is picked; 6.5 keeps the per-brush settings, size ring and [ ] keys. A note has been logged on 6.5 saying so.

Trap: rendering tiles must go through the same stroke rendering in PhotonzRender as the canvas (DryMedia and whatever each medium task adds), with a fixed seed per tile so tiles do not shimmer between renders; cache per brush, settings and colour with a limit (objectives: every cache has a limit).
acceptance: Built to the mock docs/design/mocks/pages/brush-library.html (and the brush picking parts of brush-editor.html): the brush library is the Library panel group with its scope set to Brushes, with the mock's groups, and a compact chooser opened from the brush in the tool options over the tool bar shows the same tiles; any departure from the mock is a decision card, never a quiet rewrite

Each tile is a sample stroke rendered by the real brush engine at that brush's settings in the current foreground colour, never a stored picture; changing the colour repaints the tiles; tiles render without a visible stall (time to fill the grid MEASURED in the audit)
Picking a tile arms that brush, the next stroke paints with it, its own settings show in the tool options and the panel, and the canvas sample stroke (where the mock has one) repaints
The Medium dropdown is gone from the tool options; every brush in the app (including any added later, such as Pencil) shows up as a tile without a second list in the app

Keyboard: the chooser opens from the tool options, arrows move between tiles, Return picks, Escape closes; a walk with no flags picks two different brushes by clicking tiles at a point on their face and paints with each

Audit under queue/audits/ with a picture of the library and the compact chooser beside the mock, and the strokes painted after each pick; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
